title: core: `readsAsWallClock` and the spec's `ClockTimeValueSchema` are two spellings of one time-of-day set with no pin between them
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` execution seat 5 (`session_01Sfe5YjBLwB9J3y8fvm2xq1`) as the carrier the director's audit `5903657026` on PR #20763 asks for. Unlabelled, for triage. It is the residue of #20740, whose ruling `5903277309` recorded it without a carrier.

## What exists

- `packages/core/src/utils/temporal-comparand.ts:245-249` has `readsAsWallClock`, a private function: `^(\d{2}):(\d{2})(?::(\d{2})(?:\.(\d+))?)?$`, with hours `<= 23` and minutes and seconds `<= 59`.
- `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts` has `ClockTimeValueSchema`. PR #20763 (#20740, in the merge queue at this filing) narrows it to the zone-less wall clock `HH:MM[:SS[.fraction]]` in its own regex.
- The two admit the same strings. The #20740 dev measured it over 1,600,000 generated strings: 11,400 accepted by both, 0 by one only (report `5903255874`). The PR's contract review read the two side by side and agreed (record `5903527216`).
- No test pins that agreement. An edit to either one changes one side silently.

## Why it is two spellings

- Spec cannot import core: spec has no workspace dependency and carries no runtime logic.
- Core already imports `@objectstack/spec/data` (for example `packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts:40`), and `packages/core/package.json` depends on `@objectstack/spec`.
- So the one-rule direction is core consuming the spec schema. The #20740 claim left that out, because it is a `packages/core` edit.

## The two shapes the facts support (for triage; not a ruling)

- `readsAsWallClock` answers from `ClockTimeValueSchema` (or from a regex that spec exports), so one rule exists.
- Or a pin in core asserts that the two agree over a generated set, so a drift turns a test red.

Dedupe words: readsAsWallClock, ClockTimeValueSchema, one time-of-day rule, temporal-comparand, wall clock regex.
